S1.why: Two words under the bracket; the tiles above already show what is free, so no noun is needed.

S2.why: An invitation in the du form, exactly 20 characters. It names what the person gets and says nothing about a limit. Comma before the clause because the vocabulary sentence uses the start comma.

S3.s: Du har brugt dine %lld gratis Cutlings. De bliver ved med at virke, helt gratis.
S3.back: You have used your 5 free Cutlings. They keep on at working, completely free.
S3.why: Cutlings is the vocabulary's item word, capitalised as in its count and list title. "Bliver ved med at virke" is how a Dane says keeps working; "helt gratis" carries that they stay free. 77 characters.

S4.why: Plain statement in du form; gratis goes last, the way it falls in speech.

S5.s: %lld af dine %lld gratis Cutlings er brugt.
S5.back: 3 of your 5 free Cutlings are used.
S5.why: Danish keeps the English order (used, then total), so plain %lld twice works. "Af" takes the plural noun, so it reads right for 1 too. Uses brugt, as S3 does.

S6.why: "Plads til" is the everyday Danish for room for. %@ arrives as 5.000, and with it the line is exactly 24 characters.

S7.s: Gem op til %@ tekster og %lld billeder.
S7.back: Save up to 5.000 texts and 500 images.
S7.why: Builds on the vocabulary's Tekst and Billeder (plural tekster, lowercase mid-sentence); the imperative keeps the grey line short.

S8.why: Danish lists three things with "og" and no comma before it; Apple's product names stay as they are.

S9.s: Ét køb gælder på alle tre, når de er logget ind på din Apple-konto.
S9.back: One purchase applies on all three, when they are logged in on your Apple-account.
S9.why: "Logget ind på din Apple-konto" comes straight from the vocabulary sentence. Ét takes the accent to mark the numeral. 67 characters.

S10.why: The plain Danish for a single payment; én is accented so it reads as the number.

S11.s: Intet abonnement, ingen reklamer og ingen tilmelding.
S11.back: No subscription, no advertisements and no sign-up.
S11.why: Intet/ingen agree with neuter abonnement and common reklamer/tilmelding, joined by "og" with no serial comma. Tilmelding is the Danish word for signing up. 53 characters.

S12.why: Danish iOS apps and the App Store use this wording for the restore action, so it is the one people recognise.

S13.why: Present tense of the same verb, ending in the ellipsis character.

S14.why: "Låse op" is the Danish unlock. With the object between the verb and op, "for" can only mean the price; "Lås op for %@" would read as unlock the price. 21 characters plus the price.

S15.why: The same action without a price, exactly 14 characters.

S16.why: Danish iOS uses this to put something off without refusing it.

S17.why: The verb Danish iOS uses on its close buttons.

S18.why: Warm and plain; "det hele" means all of it, the room included. Neuter dit agrees with det. 18 characters.

S19.s: Tak for dit køb. Det støtter Cutling og den ene person, der laver appen.
S19.back: Thanks for your purchase. It supports Cutling and the one person, who makes the-app.
S19.why: "Tak for dit køb" is how Danish shops say thanks. "Den ene person" stresses one single maker. Appen avoids saying Cutling twice.

S20.s: Velkommen tilbage. Dit køb er gendannet.
S20.back: Welcome back. Your purchase is restored.
S20.why: Gendannet ties back to the Gendan køb link the person tapped; short and friendly.

S21.why: Spoken form of S5, without dine and the full stop; plural after af works for any count.

S22.s: Du har gemt %lld, og nu er der plads til %@ Cutlings.
S22.back: You have saved 5, and now is there room for 5.000 Cutlings.
S22.why: No noun follows %lld, so it is right for 1, 2, 5 and 21 with no plural rule. The noun follows %@, which is always plural.

S23.s: Cutling er låst op. Nu er der plads til %@ Cutlings.
S23.back: Cutling is locked up. Now is there room for 5.000 Cutlings.
S23.why: "Låst op" is the participle of låse op; the second sentence repeats S6's plads til phrasing so VoiceOver and the screen agree.

S24.why: Calm passive, so it blames nobody; gennemført is the usual Danish for a transaction that went through. 26 characters.

S25.s: Der er ingen forbindelse til App Store lige nu. Prøv igen om lidt.
S25.back: There is no connection to App Store right now. Try again in a little.
S25.why: "Ingen forbindelse" is how Danish says it can't be reached; "om lidt" means shortly. 66 characters.

S26.s: App Store har ikke bekræftet købet.
S26.back: App Store has not confirmed the-purchase.
S26.why: Says only what happened, with App Store as the subject, so the person is not blamed.

S27.s: Der er intet køb af Cutling på den Apple-konto, der er logget ind her.
S27.back: There is no purchase of Cutling on the Apple-account, that is logged in here.
S27.why: "Logget ind" echoes the vocabulary sentence; "her" stands for this device, as Danish speech does, and keeps it to 70 characters.

S28.s: Den gratis version rummer %lld Cutlings. Lås Cutling op én gang, så kan du gemme så mange, du vil.
S28.back: The free version holds 5 Cutlings. Lock Cutling up one time, then can you save as many, you want.
S28.why: Rummer is the natural verb for holding a number of things. "…, så kan du" is how a Dane links an action to its result. 95 characters.

S29.why: Compact pair matching S1's "5 gratis"; the list title above names the items. 13 characters.

K1.s: Alle %lld gratis er brugt. Tryk og lås op
K1.back: All 5 free are used. Tap and unlock
K1.why: "Tryk og lås op" is spoken Danish for tap to unlock and fits the one-key capsule: exactly 38 characters. Gratis stands as a noun here, which Danish allows.

M1.why: A verb-led command name, like Danish Mac window titles; the same words as the iPhone button S15.

M2.why: M1 as a button, with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label using the vocabulary's capitalised item word.

M4.why: Danish says a count pair with "af"; 6 characters.

M5.why: The same status words as S23, so Mac and iPhone say it the same way.

M6.s: Ét køb låser Cutling op på iPhone, iPad og Mac.
M6.back: One purchase locks Cutling up on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Uses S8's list and the låse op verb; Ét is accented for the numeral.

M7.s: Låst op på iPhone, iPad og Mac med denne Apple-konto.
M7.back: Locked up on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple-account.
M7.why: Status phrase with no subject, as a settings caption usually has; Apple-konto is the vocabulary's spelling.

M8.s: Du købte Cutling, før den blev gratis, så den er og bliver låst op. Tak for din støtte.
M8.back: You bought Cutling, before it became free, so it is and remains locked up. Thanks for your support.
M8.why: "Er og bliver" is the idiomatic Danish for stays that way for good; the thanks is short and plain. 87 characters.
